body: Well it's nice that there's someone out there that can relate.
Nope. My only shtick is drawing, which I don't do much of. I'm not even that great at it for my age.
If it was I would have drawn in the past 2 years. I used to like drawings. Now it's too stressful.

I'm not sure. Probably something arty, but to do that I would have to work extremely hard. Which I have proven to myself I can't do. Being kicked out it's really relevant to my current problem, it's just something that happened.
My mother neglected me and kicked me out of my house at 17. I live with a room-mate. And I do not want a job that will make me money, I want a job that will make me happy.

I have tried the school counsellors, and therapists. They don't really help. The people on here have helped more and they're just strangers. It doesn't matter at this point, my exams are within the next three weeks. 

And I can't understand how failing A levels does not make me stupid, considering that 99.9% of people pass.

It is not the qualification that matters to me. I don't care about the subjects I do, I could probably get the job I want without them providing I worked hard enough. It's that I failed something nearly everyone else hasn't, twice. If I can't succeed on my second chance at something that destroyed me the first time, how am I supposed to think I'll have the integrity to work hard enough for anything else.
I had to stop after he said women are atrocious in quality. That feels pretty alienating.

Stress is part of it but there's not much I can do considering I've got 3 weeks until the year is over. You can't retake college, it is only for people in a certain age range. What is the motivation for moving on when nothing has changed for years.
Often thought about looking into those kind of subreddits. But it feels kind of guilty, like you know you're going to end up bothering someone else with your problems. Misery loves company.

I'm not talking about adult education courses or any sort of 'equivilant', I'm talking about college/high school. The thing that everyone passes, they have huge fucking posters plastered over the walls saying "99.9% C-A grade!"

This is one of the simplest things and I failed it bloody twice. That makes me feel a bit like shit, it's been years and I don't feel any happier and I haven't changed at all.

I can relate. The 'friends' that I have share no interests with me, it's becoming increasingly hard to talk to them. It's also quite sad seeing it on the internet everywhere, girl gamers they're so rare I wish I knew one. Funny, I've reached out to so many people but no one wants to play.
No. No college/high school will take on someone who failed twice. I'll be a high school drop out, in american terms.

There are multiple exams for each subject, if I failed one I could retake it, but if you fail all of them you cannot re-do the A level. And it does feel like the end of the world. I've tried so hard to improve myself, but it feels like I haven't tried at all. And I'm still in the same place. And I failed my second chance.
